title: REVIEW of the new and (hopefully) Broadway-bound musical Swept Away, ...
transcript: First theater review of 2024. And we have to talk about Swift away. Swift Away is a new jukebox musical by the Ava Brothers. And yes, it is a jukebox, which I did not realize going in. But I was not familiar with the music of the Ava Brothers before going into the show, so it was basically a new score for me. And I have to say, I really loved the music in the show. It's such a unique, folksy sound with a little bit of, like, sea shanty thrown in. It is just one of those shows where I walked out and immediately was like, I need a cast recording. Also to shout out the performances, especially John Gallagher, Jr, who I think is giving his best performance in Spring Awakening. And if this does come to Broadway, I definitely expect him to be into any consideration. But then we have the subject matter of the show itself. And this show was so much darker than I expected it to be. And to be fair, I probably should have expected that, because I did know that this was a show about a shipwreck. But I kind of expected them to get shipwrecked on an island, like in so many shipwreck stories. But no, they are stranded in the middle of the ocean with no food, no water for what could be an indefinite period of time. And as you can imagine, the psychological tool that this takes on Them and the length that they must go to in order to survive are very real and very visceral. They have to say, one thing this production really nails is that feeling of isolation. This is especially captured well in the scenic design. And while I won't spoil anything, there's one scene transition that is really, really cool and one of the highlights of the show. I do have to wonder, is a show with this kind of subject matter something that could be commercially successful on Broadway? Because not only is it a different style of music than most Broadway audiences are used to, it's also just a really dark story and that's gonna be a tough sell to general audiences. But I also look at the success of something like Hades Town, which also had a folk inspired score that was different from the usual Broadway sound. And they also have a somewhat depressing subject matter and they've been able to find commercial success. And so maybe there is a place for booked away on Broadway. And I really hope that if they do choose to come to Broadway, it does find that commercial success, cause I think this is a really, really great show. With all that said, I'm going to give it a 4 out of five stars. Definitely recommend checking it out if you are in the DC area. Is running through January 14th only, so not a lot of time left. But hopefully this is Not the last that we'll see of the show
reasoning: Clear recommendation with 4/5 stars, strong praise for music, performances, and design. Minor caveats about commercial viability don't undercut the enthusiastic endorsement.
